cohort: The study included 100 preeclampsia patients requiring induction of labor, divided into two groups of 50 for different induction methods.
finding: Low dose misoprostol (25 mcg) was concluded to be a cheap and effective drug for cervical ripening and labour induction in pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Misoprostol demonstrated a higher vaginal delivery rate (76%) and a lower caesarean section rate (24%) compared to dinoprostone (66% vaginal, 34% C-section), though this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.7496).
